title: chore(claude): allow dev commits and card-branch pushes
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

## What changes

`.claude/settings.json`:

- `permissions.allow` gains two entries:
  ```
  "Bash(git commit -F *)",
  "Bash(git push -u origin claude/issue-*)"
  ```
- A new `permissions.ask` list holds three entries scoped to those two rules, so that only the bare forms run without approval. Ask takes precedence over allow.
  ```
  "Bash(git commit -F * *)",
  "Bash(git push -u origin claude/issue-* *)",
  "Bash(git push -u origin claude/issue-*:*)"
  ```

## Why

The maintainer chose to allow these durably on 2026-11-19 (in the data-2 thread), and agreed at 09:25Z to the seat opening this PR. Card developers' commits on two card branches (#35401, #35047) were stopped for an approval no one was present to give. The maintainer merges this PR himself.

## Reach

- **Runs without approval:** exactly `git commit -F FILE` and `git push -u origin claude/issue-BRANCH`, the forms os-dev uses.
- **Still asks:** anything after the message file (for example `-a`, `--amend`, `-n`, `--no-verify` or a pathspec), anything after the card branch (a second refspec, a tag, a force, delete, prune or mirror flag, `--no-verify`), and a `src:dst` refspec on the card branch.
- **Spelling:** a message file path containing a space also asks, because the matcher reads the space as "something after". A push or commit spelt any other way (`-m`, a bare `git push`) still asks, as today.
- **Chained lines:** a line that starts with either allowed form and continues (for example the commit chained to the push, or the push piped into `tail`) asks, because ask rules are tried against the whole line. Developers type each command on its own.
- **Commit spelling:** os-dev.md names no commit spelling yet; a follow-up adds `git commit -F FILE` there.
- **Other sessions:** every rule starts with the allowed command's own prefix, so no push or commit outside these two forms changes behaviour.
- **Unchanged:** `main`'s ruleset (merge queue, no force-push, no deletion), the `deny` roster (17 GitHub content-write tools) and the hooks.

## Verification

- `node scripts/pm/check-settings-deny-roster.mjs` passes locally.
- The file parses as JSON.
- The contract review records (round 1, delta 1) are on this PR, and a delta on this head follows.
